feedback.problem:
Find the exact value of $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{12}).$

*Hint: Use the fact that $-\frac{\pi }{12}=\frac{\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{3}.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the difference formula for cosine with $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ and $y=\frac{\pi }{3},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{12}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
